pr_title: fix(rust, python): Set correct dtype for `.extract_groups()`

issue_context.title: str.extract_groups wrong lazy dtype
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.


### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl

df = pl.LazyFrame(
    data={
        "url": [
            "http://vote.com/ballon_dor?candidate=messi&ref=python",
            "http://vote.com/ballon_dor?candidate=weghorst&ref=polars",
            "http://vote.com/ballon_dor?error=404&ref=rust",
        ]
    }
)
pattern = r"candidate=(?<candidate>\w+)&ref=(?<ref>\w+)"
df = df.select(captures=pl.col("url").str.extract_groups(pattern)).unnest("captures")

assert df.schema == {"candidate": pl.Utf8, "ref": pl.Utf8}
```


### Issue description

Super cool that `str.extract_groups` finally made it in PR #10179!

However it's broken on lazy frames due to a incorrect return dtype.

In the example, the `unnest` crashes because `extract_groups` is returning the default `{'captures': pl.Utf8}` dtype.

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "bug.py", line 18, in <module>
    assert df.schema == {"candidate": pl.Utf8, "ref": pl.Utf8}
           ^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/python/3.11.3/lib/python3.11/site-packages/polars/lazyframe/frame.py", line 628, in schema
    return self._ldf.schema()
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
exceptions.SchemaError: expected struct dtype, got: `str`
```

### Expected behavior

`df.schema` should be `{"candidate": pl.Utf8, "ref": pl.Utf8}`

The other `.str` function I know that returns a struct is `str.splitn` which lives elsewhere:

https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/bfabdd50639b271da45027809cf720771e3c6685/crates/polars-plan/src/dsl/string.rs#L347

I'm guessing this is what generates the "dynamic schema"

https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/bfabdd50639b271da45027809cf720771e3c6685/crates/polars-plan/src/dsl/string.rs#L387

Does this mean if something returns a struct it cannot live inside `/function_expr/`?

review_comments: We now can use the names available in the `DataType::Struct`
No need to allocate a string here?
Yep, thanks. Need to become more aware regarding allocations.

determining the data type here, means we only do that computation of the data type once. 

The regex is compiled twice, because we cannot send the regex in the logical plan.

In the previous commit we would compile the regex every time we ask the schema, which we do a lot.

Thanks @ritchie46 - makes sense once you see it.

I think one of the issues I was having was not understanding the order of operations fully.

`dsl/string.rs` -> `function_expr/strings.rs`

So I wasn't able to figure out at what point one could manipulate the dtype (other than what I initially tried)
